summary: Junmai Zhang (1886–1969) was a scholar in philosophy and sinology. He studied under Qichao Liang (~1902–1906), at Waseda University (~1906–1910), and the University of Berlin (~1913–1915), later holding posts at Peking University and Tsinghua University.

Junsho Kato (b. 1934) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Akira Hirakawa, Étienne Lamotte, Juntaka Kato, and Hajime Nakamura, earning a PhD from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Nishogakusha, Nagoya, and Reitaku Universities.

Juntarō Ishihama (1888–1968) worked in sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Kansai University (~1906–1908), he held academic posts at Ryukoku University (~1921–1948) and Kansai University (~1949–1960).
Junzo Inagaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoshin Fukihara. He served as section chief (課長) at the Otani University Library.
Junzo Tanizawa is a philosopher who served as a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 1987) and assistant professor at Shinshu University (attested 2000).
Juri Lotman (1922–1993) was a linguist who studied at the University of Saint Petersburg between 1939 and 1961. He held a post at the University of Tartu beginning in 1954.

Shigeaki Watanabe worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, having studied under Gerhard Oberhammer. He held posts at the University of Tsukuba (attested 1989–1990) and Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies as professor (attested 2003).
Jushu Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Bukkyo University as a part-time lecturer (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).

Justin McDaniel (b. 1972) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts at the University of California, Riverside as associate professor and at the University of Pennsylvania as professor of religious studies (attested 2011–2018).

Justin Ritzinger specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett, and has held posts at Oberlin College, Dharma Drum Mountain, Dharma Drum Institute, and Academia Sinica.
Justin Shimeld is a philosopher who completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania (attested 2012) under the supervision of Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.
Justus Günther Grassmann (1779–1852) studied at the University of Halle (~1797–1801) and held a post at Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1806 to 1852.

Justus Olshausen (1800–1882) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Kiel, Berlin, and Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, Langlès, and Kieffer, later holding posts at Kiel University, the University of Königsberg, and Prussian institutions.
Jyotirindranath Tagore (1849–1925) was active in linguistics and other fields. He completed his studies at Hindu School and Presidency University (~1864–1867).

János Szerb (1951–1988) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Eötvös Loránd University (~1975–1980), he held posts at the University of Vienna (1982) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (~1983–1988).

Jérôme Ducor (b. 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Jacques May. He held positions at the University of Lausanne (~2001) and the International Association of Buddhist Studies (~2005–2014).

Józef Maria Bocheński (1902–1995) was a philosopher who studied at Jagiellonian University, the University of Fribourg, and the Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas. He held academic posts at the Pontifical University (~1934–1940) and the University of Fribourg (~1945–1972).

Józef Szczepan Kowalewski (1800–1878) was an Iranian, Central Asian, Buddhist, and linguistics scholar. Educated at Vilnius and Kazan under Groddeck, Khalfin, Erdmann, Kazembek, and Igumnov, he held professorships and leadership roles at Kazan Federal University and the University of Warsaw.
Józef Turczyński (1884–1953) held posts at the Ukrainian National Academy of Music (~1914–1919) and the Chopin University of Music (~1920–1939), where he taught Constantin Régamey.

József Budenz (1836–1892) was a linguist who studied at Marburg and Göttingen, the latter under Theodor Benfey. He worked at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (1861) and served as professor of Altaic comparative linguistics at Eötvös Loránd University (1868–1892).
